nutshell: A broad market sell-off driven by economic slowdown fears and anxiety in the tech sector.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the closing bell report for February 5th. The market finished the day with a broad and significant sell-off.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. It was a tough day, with all the major indices falling more than 1%. The S&P 500 closed down 1.23% at 6,798, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 1.59% to finish at 22,540. Today's market can be summed up as a broad decline driven by concerns over an economic slowdown and anxiety in the tech sector. Weaker-than-expected jobs data heightened worries about a recession, and at the same time, unease about corporate earnings forecasts put a chill on investor sentiment.

sources.title: JOLTS Job Openings
Stocks tumble on weak labor market data and AI concerns

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Doesn't a cooling job market usually boost hopes for a Fed rate cut, which is good for stocks? Why did the market react the opposite way today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's an excellent point. It's because the market's focus has shifted from the Fed's interest rate policy to the actual health of the real economy. The December job openings figure released today came in well below expectations, falling to its lowest level since 2020. Previously, the market hoped for the labor market to cool off to help tame inflation. But now, the fear is that it has gone too far and could lead to a slowdown or even a recession. On top of that, in the tech sector, concerns are rising that AI advancements could actually harm the business models of existing software companies. We also saw stocks like Amazon fall despite strong earnings due to worries about future investment costs, which added to the market's overall decline.

sources.title: JOLTS Job Openings
Anthropic's AI push raises analyst concerns over IT services revenues

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So concerns about both the economy and corporate earnings weighed on the market. Could you break down the key factors that moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, we can really break it down into three main themes today. First, the economic slowdown fears sparked by weaker-than-expected jobs data. Second, the impact on tech stocks from a potential shake-up in the AI industry. And finally, the pressure from some disappointing corporate outlooks and a sharp drop in Bitcoin. Let's dive into each of these one by one.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with that first point you mentioned: the employment data. As you said, news that the market might normally welcome was met with the complete opposite reaction today.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, the market's interpretation has completely flipped. Today's JOLTS report showed December job openings at 6.54 million, well below the 7.2 million expected and the lowest since September 2020. Adding to that, weekly initial jobless claims came in higher than anticipated at 231,000, suggesting the labor market isn't just cooling, but potentially freezing. On this news, the S&P 500 fell over 1.2% and the Nasdaq dropped nearly 1.6%. Concerns about a slowdown completely overshadowed any hopes for rate cuts. The 10-year Treasury yield, a classic safe haven, fell to 4.21%, while the VIX, the market's fear gauge, surged over 16% to cross the 21 mark. This indicates that market participants are now seriously starting to price in the risk of a recession.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, should we take this to mean the market is now weighing the bad news of a potential recession more heavily than the good news of a potential Fed rate cut?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. It seems we've entered a phase where 'bad news is just bad news.' For a while, the market reacted positively to a cooling labor market, seeing it as a sign of easing inflation. But now, the perception is that we've crossed a critical threshold. We saw a clear defensive rotation in the market today. The Industrials sector fell over 2% and Consumer Discretionary was also weak. In contrast, Utilities, a classic defensive play, finished slightly higher, and Consumer Staples saw only minor losses. This is clear evidence that investors are adjusting their portfolios in anticipation of a future economic contraction. The Challenger, Gray & Christmas report showing January layoff plans were the highest since 2009 only amplified fears that business sentiment is already freezing over.

sources.title: Stocks tumble on weak labor market data and AI concerns

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: It's a bit surprising then, with this flight to safety, that precious metals like gold and silver fell today. How should we interpret that?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It's a very unusual phenomenon, and it shows the market's complex psychology. Typically, precious metals like gold rally on slowdown fears. But today, gold fell 2.9%, and silver, which is more sensitive to industrial demand, plunged over 16%. This suggests that the fear of a sharp contraction in overall industrial demand, should a recession hit, is outweighing the simple safe-haven appeal. A slightly stronger dollar index also put pressure on precious metals. In the end, it seems investors felt they had nowhere to hide but in bonds, reflecting a very pessimistic scenario that goes beyond simple risk aversion to pricing in a potential sharp contraction in the real economy.

sources.title: Stocks tumble on weak labor market data and AI concerns

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So looking ahead, what should we be watching to get a sense of the market's direction?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The market's focus will now shift from employment to consumer and inflation data. We need to see if the weakening labor market translates into weaker consumer sentiment and a real drop in demand. The upcoming Retail Sales data on February 10th and the Consumer Price Index on February 13th will be critical turning points. If retail sales also show a slowdown, recession fears will spread further. On the other hand, if inflation remains high, the Fed will be stuck in a difficult position between stimulating the economy and controlling prices. The bond market, with the 10-year yield falling, is already pricing in a higher probability of a slowdown, but the market's direction will become clearer after these two reports are released.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Along with those economic slowdown fears, the other major factor shaking the market today was anxiety in the tech sector. Specifically, this growing concern that AI advancements could actually hurt existing companies. Can you break that down for us?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, today really showed tech investors the double-edged sword of AI. The Nasdaq fell 1.59%, taking a bigger hit than the S&P 500's 1.31% drop, and the tech-focused XLK ETF led the market lower, falling over 2%. The direct cause was the release of a new AI model from Anthropic, an AI company backed by Amazon and Google. This sparked fears that the new technology could cannibalize the existing software industry. As a result, shares of Palantir, a key AI-related stock, dropped over 6.5%. The VIX surged more than 13%, and we saw a classic risk-off move as investors fled to the safety of Treasuries, pushing the 10-year yield down.

sources.title: Anthropic releases AI upgrade as market punishes software stocks

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it's not that AI technology is failing, but the exact opposite—the fear that it's becoming so successful it could disrupt the existing industry structure is what's dragging down stocks.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Precisely. A fear of so-called 'creative destruction' has swept the market. Anthropic's new AI model can automate professional tasks like reviewing contracts or ensuring compliance, which directly threatens the core business models of IT consulting firms like Accenture and software-as-a-service companies like Salesforce and ServiceNow. In fact, today Accenture fell 3.4%, Salesforce dropped 3%, and ServiceNow plunged over 5.7%, directly reflecting these market concerns. Some on Wall Street are even talking about the 'end of the license model,' warning of long-term profitability erosion as AI begins to replace sophisticated tasks, meaning companies may no longer need to buy expensive software licenses for every user.

sources.title: Anthropic's AI push raises analyst concerns over IT services revenues
Anthropic’s AI Tools Rattle Software Stocks, Prompt Rethink of Sector Valuations

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So are the Big Tech companies leading AI development, like Microsoft and Google, immune to this trend?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The fact that they aren't is what adds to the complexity of the problem. Microsoft and Google also couldn't escape the impact, falling over 1.8% and 2.2% respectively. While these companies are at the forefront of AI technology, they also have massive existing software and cloud businesses to protect. They're caught in a dilemma: as the competition between Anthropic and OpenAI intensifies, they're spending astronomical amounts on AI model development and data center expansion, yet this very technology could end up cannibalizing their existing revenue streams. Investors are now starting to weigh two risks simultaneously: the huge upfront investment costs and the potential for this new tech to erode their current businesses, rather than just focusing on the future promise of AI.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it seems uncertainty has peaked over how this massive wave of AI will reshape the entire tech landscape.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. The market is moving past the phase of viewing all tech stocks positively under the 'AI' banner and is now trying to distinguish the true winners and losers of the AI era. Some analysts see this not as a short-term panic, but as the beginning of a 'structural repricing'—a fundamental reassessment of valuations across the entire software industry. Going forward, the key determinant for tech stock performance will be their ability to prove, in their earnings reports, how they are using AI to cut costs, generate new revenue, and defend their existing businesses.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: On top of the macroeconomic anxiety and concerns about structural shifts in tech, it sounds like disappointing outlooks from some companies and a sharp drop in Bitcoin also fueled the sell-off.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that's right. It was a day where bad news from individual companies triggered a chain reaction, fueling broader risk-off sentiment. With December job openings falling to a post-2020 low and stoking slowdown fears, the VIX, the market's fear gauge, surged over 22% to break above 20. While safe-haven demand was strong, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.21%, we saw the unusual sight of even precious metals selling off, with gold down 2.3% and silver plunging over 13%. Adding to this, Bitcoin's price fell below $67,000 during the session, sending a shockwave through the crypto market and contributing to the Nasdaq's drop of over 1.7%. Ultimately, the market reacted more sensitively to future uncertainty than to the present value of corporate earnings.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: And with Amazon specifically, its earnings weren't actually bad, yet the stock fell sharply. What was the reason for that?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Amazon reported solid Q4 results, with revenue topping $213.3 billion, beating expectations, and EPS also coming in strong at $1.95. The problem was the massive investment plan announced after the report. CEO Andy Jassy revealed that the company plans to spend around $200 billion on capital expenditures in 2026 alone, focusing on AI, robotics, and its satellite internet business. This figure was far beyond Wall Street's expectations of around $140-150 billion, amplifying concerns among investors about short-term cash flow and profitability. In the end, despite the solid earnings, the weight of future investment costs dragged the stock down over 4.4%.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: The sharp drop in Bitcoin also had a significant impact on related company stocks, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, Bitcoin was another major mover today. As its price fell below $70,000, stocks of companies holding large amounts of Bitcoin plunged in tandem. A prime example is MicroStrategy. The company's strategy of incorporating Bitcoin as a primary corporate asset has made it a de facto proxy for Bitcoin itself. When Bitcoin's price tumbled, coinciding with its earnings release, the stock plummeted by over 17%. MicroStrategy reported a Q4 operating loss of $17.4 billion and a net loss of $12.4 billion, which reflects the write-down in the value of its Bitcoin holdings on its books. The volatility in the crypto market clearly weighed on broader tech investor sentiment.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Were there any companies that managed to do well in this difficult market environment?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Of course. And by looking at the companies that moved against the market tide, we can get a glimpse of what investors are focusing on. For example, home fitness company Peloton plunged more than 25% after reporting weak results and announcing the resignation of its CFO. Its Q4 revenue of $656.5 million missed estimates, and its loss per share of 9 cents was wider than expected. On the other hand, online gaming platform Roblox saw its shares surge in after-hours trading after reporting a smaller-than-expected loss of 45 cents per share and revenue of $1.42 billion that beat estimates. Ultimately, with uncertainty on the rise, the market was unforgiving to companies with conservative outlooks or disappointing results, but it generously rewarded those that exceeded expectations. It was a day where sorting the winners from the losers was very apparent.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, as you said, it was clearly a stock-picker's market. And in this kind of choppy environment, one of the most divisive stocks has to be Tesla. It was extremely volatile today but ended up finishing flat. What was behind those big swings during the session?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, Tesla's stock movement today was a microcosm of the fierce debate surrounding the company right now. After rallying to around $402 early in the session, it plunged to about $387 before closing near its opening price. This extreme volatility is because the views on Tesla's present and future are sharply divided. On one hand, concerns are weighing on the stock about the deteriorating fundamentals of its core business, with 2025 annual net income nearly halved from the previous year and Volkswagen overtaking it as the top EV seller in Europe. On the other hand, the expectation that this is just a growing pain on its path to becoming an AI platform company is still supporting the stock.

sources.title: Volkswagen overtook Tesla as Europe's top EV seller in 2025

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you mentioned, the bulls have consistently argued that Tesla should be viewed as an AI company, not just a car company. Is that growth story still considered valid?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Investors who focus on its growth potential emphasize that very point. They interpret the current earnings decline as a deliberate process to pour massive capital into future technologies like the Robotaxi and the Optimus humanoid robot. In fact, in its 10-K filing, Tesla defines itself as a company that 'implements real-world AI' and states that it already launched its Robotaxi service in June 2025. From this perspective, the car is not the final product but merely a device for collecting data to train its self-driving AI. Therefore, falling behind in the short-term car sales race is irrelevant; the logic is that through these investments, Tesla can dominate the massive future markets of transportation and robotic labor.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: That's a very powerful future vision. But on the flip side of that rosy outlook, what are the specific risk factors that have investors concerned?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The concerns from the other side are very real and specific. The biggest issue is the risky capital allocation strategy of pouring money from a faltering core business into new ventures with uncertain success. Net income in 2025 plummeted to $3.8 billion, yet capital expenditures on property, plant, and equipment in the same year were more than double that at $8.5 billion. There are warnings that if this continues, free cash flow could be depleted within one or two years. Even more serious are the legal risks. As stated in the 10-K report, the company is under investigation by the Department of Justice and the SEC regarding its Full Self-Driving capabilities. This is seen as an existential threat that could lead to billions in fines and business suspension, similar to Volkswagen's 'Dieselgate' scandal.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the market is essentially caught in a tug-of-war between deteriorating current performance and the uncertain potential for future success. How should we weigh these two conflicting views?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Ultimately, the situation right now seems to be one where the tangible risks outweigh the potential opportunities. The growth story is based on the company's declarations and future possibilities, whereas the risk factors are grounded in objective facts: the deteriorating performance recorded in current financial statements, specific legal risks disclosed in official reports, and the rise of competitors. The concern is that before the future of Robotaxis or Optimus becomes a reality, the foundation of the core business could crumble and unbearable legal liabilities could materialize, potentially causing permanent damage to the company's value. Therefore, it seems to be a time for a cautious approach, questioning whether the current stock price fully reflects these specific risks.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Could you please summarize today's market action and point out what we should be watching for going forward?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, all three major indices finished lower today as hopes for a Fed rate cut faded. A much stronger-than-expected ISM Services PMI, combined with cautious remarks from Chair Jerome Powell, led the market to pull back its expectations for an early rate cut. The surge in Treasury yields particularly hit the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which saw the steepest decline.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So what are the key variables that will determine the market's direction in the near term?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Ultimately, all eyes will be on the two things that will drive the Fed's decision: jobs and inflation data. First, we need to watch the non-farm payrolls report coming out next week on the 11th. Given that last week's jobs report shocked the market by coming in much hotter than expected, the key question will be whether the labor market remains strong. The unemployment rate and average hourly earnings will be released at the same time, and if wage pressures don't show signs of easing, the Fed's dilemma will only deepen.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: And besides jobs, inflation data is also critical, right? We have a report scheduled for that as well?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. On the 13th, we'll get the Consumer Price Index, or CPI. While the inflation trend has been slowing thanks to recent drops in oil prices and stable goods prices, the concern is that service inflation, like housing costs, remains stubbornly high. The market will be looking to this CPI report for confirmation that inflation is smoothly heading towards the Fed's 2% target. We also need to keep an eye on the 30-year bond auction results on the 12th and the FOMC minutes, which will be released on the 18th, as they could provide important clues about the Fed's policy path.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it looks like we're in for a period of data-watching as we try to anticipate the Fed's next move. Finally, do you have any closing thoughts for our listeners?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, it looks like this tug-of-war between the market and the Fed will continue. This could be a period of heightened volatility, so rather than making hasty predictions, it would be prudent to calmly assess the incoming data as it's released.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: That concludes our closing bell report for February 5th. Thank you.
